result.paraphrase: The rapid rise in breast cancer cases worldwide has prompted academia and industry to develop a more effective and robust computer-aided diagnosis (BC-CAD) system for breast cancer detection. Several methods have been proposed, focusing on case-centric segmentation, feature extraction, and classification of breast cancer histopathological images. However, increasing complexity and the need for higher accuracy often require a stronger solution. Recently, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have emerged as one of the most effective techniques for medical data analysis and various image classification problems. In this paper, a highly robust and efficient BC-CAD solution is proposed. The system includes preprocessing, an enhanced adaptive-learning Gaussian mixture model (GMM), connected-component-analysis-based region-of-interest localization, and AlexNet-DNN-based feature extraction. Principal component analysis (PCA) and linear discriminant analysis (LDA) are used for feature selection as dimensionality reduction. One advantage of the proposed method is that it does not use existing dimensionality reduction algorithms employed with SVM for breast cancer detection and classification. Overall results show that AlexNet-DNN features from the fully connected layer, with FC6 plus LDA dimensional reduction and SVM-based classification, outperform other state-of-the-art methods for breast cancer detection. The proposed approach achieved 96.20 for AlexNet-FC6 and 96.70 for AlexNet-FC7 in the evaluation measures.
